principle.name: DRY - Don't Repeat Yourself
principle.description: Eliminate code duplication through abstraction and reuse
principle.rationale: Duplicated code increases maintenance burden and bug risk

example.good: Extract common logic into a helper function or trait

principle.name: SOLID - Single Responsibility
principle.description: Each module/function should have one reason to change

example.scenario: A function that validates, processes, and saves data
example.good: Split into separate validation, processing, and persistence functions
example.bad: Keep all logic in one monolithic function

principle.name: SOLID - Open/Closed
principle.description: Open for extension, closed for modification
principle.rationale: Allows adding features without breaking existing code

example.good: Use traits and generics for extensibility
example.bad: Modify existing enum with new variants everywhere

principle.name: LEAN - Eliminate Waste
principle.description: Remove unnecessary code, abstractions, and complexity
principle.rationale: Waste increases cognitive load and maintenance cost

principle.name: KISS - Keep It Simple, Stupid
principle.description: Prefer simple solutions over complex ones
principle.rationale: Complexity is the enemy of maintainability

example.scenario: A simple counter vs. a complex state machine
example.good: Use simple counter when it meets requirements

guidelines.guideline: Borrow when you don't need ownership
Use references for function parameters when possible
Use iterators instead of imperative loops
Leverage derive macros for common traits
Use builder pattern for complex construction

category.name: during_refactoring
category.item: Keep tests passing after each change
